full_judgment:
2. In Civil Revision No.1919 of 2009 Rule was issued on an application for revision made by the defendant No.3 (petitioner herein) under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly, the Code) against the judgment and order dated 23-4-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Artha Rin Case No. 107 of 1995 rejecting the application dated 23-4-2009 under Order XXVI, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by defendant No. 3 petitioner to appoint an Advocate Commissioner for recording the cross-examination of the witnesses of defendant No. 3. 

 3. In Civil Revision No. 4232 of 2009 Rule was issued on an application for revision made by the petitioner under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly the Code) against the Judgment and order dated 15-9-2009 passed by Mrs Shahnaj Sultana learned Joint District Judge, and Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005 rejection the application filed by the petitioner for stay of further proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005. 

 6. In Civil Revision No. 4232 of 2009, the fact leading to the issuance to the Rule in short, is that the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2002 under Order XXI, rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly the Code) praying for release of the schedule property from Title Execution Case No. 75 of 2000 filed by opposite party No. 1. The further case of the petitioner is that he purchased the suit property after due compliance of all the necessary formalities and mutated his name. He is a bonafide purchaser with, value. Opposite party No.2 has committed fraud on opposite party No. I bank and opposite party No.3 by allegedly creating mortgage of the suit land in which he had no right title and interest to create such mortgage. The Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. has also filed a suit in the Court of 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 107 of 1995 claiming the suit property. The petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 168 of 2004 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka praying for transfer of the Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2002 in the Court of 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka for analogous hearing with the Title Suit No. 107 of 1995. On 15-9-2009, the petitioner also filed an application praying for stay of proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.3, Dhaka vide order dated 15-9-2009 rejected the said application. 

 10. Mr MA Samad, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner of Civil Revision No. 4232 of 2009, submits that the Artha Rin Adalat illegally rejected the application for stay of all further proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005. He further submits that if the further proceeding is not stayed the petitioner shall suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 11. Mr Md Imam Hasan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties of Civil Revision No. 4232 of2009, submits that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat most rightly rejected that application for stay of Miscellaneous-Case No. 9 of2005. He also submits that if further proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005 is stayed the opposite parties will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 12. We have heard the learned Advocates and perused the applications in Civil Revision No. 1919 of 2009 and Civil Revision No. 4232 of 2009 and other relevant papers. In Civil Revision No. 1919 of 2009, we find that the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application under Order XXVI, rule 1 of the Code for appointing Advocate Commissioner for recording the evidence of defendant No.3. In Civil Revision No. 4232 of 2009, the impugned order reveals that the Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application for stay of all further proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005. But the learned Joint District Judge rejected the application on 15-9-2009. There is no doubt that the impugned order dated 23-4-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat 3rd Court, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 107 of 1995 and the impugned order dated 15-9-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court Artha Rin Adalat Dhaka in MisceIlaneous Case No.9 of 2005 are interlocutory orders. The moot question is whether revision lies against the interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. There are long line of decisions both from the High Court Division and the Appellate Division that any interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged by the revisional jurisdiction of this Court. In sup- port of this contention we may rely upon eases of Serajul lslam vs Agrani Bank and another Civil Rule No. 102 (con) of 2008 (unreported), the case of Belayet Hossain vs Bank Indosuez 50 DLR 431, Hosne Ara Begum vs Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, 5 MLR (AD) 290 = 53 DLR (AD) 9, 53 DLR (AD) 9; Kazi Gowaherul Islam (KJ Islam) vs Standard Co-operative Credit Society Lid. and another 50 DLR 333, MAC-Proprietor, Mahtab- uddin Chowdhury vs Agrani Bank, 14 BLD 195 = 47 DLR 233, Syed Monjur Morshed vs Manager. Agrani Bank Ltd.14 BLC 501, and Sultana jute Mills Ltd, vs Agrani Bank and others 14 BLD (AD) 196 = 46 DLR (AD) 174. 

 13. In the case of Kazi Gowaherul Islam (KJ Islam) vs Standard Co-operative Credit Society Ltd, and another the High Court Division has held that there is a complete ouster of jurisdiction of the High Court Division for interference under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against any interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 14. In the Case of Belayet Hossain vs Bank Indosuez, the High Court Division has held that the Adalat Ain is a special legislation setting up Special Court for prompt realization of loans by financial institutions. Such a Court is a Civil Court only for limited purposes. A revisional application under section 115 of the Code against any interlocutory order passed by an Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable. 

 15. In fact, in all the case cited above both the Appellate Division and High Court Division have held that any order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is not amenable to revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division. In view of the pronouncements of the Appellate Division and the High Court Division cited above, we are constrained to hold the view that the impugned order dated 23-4-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat 3rd Court Dhaka in Artha Rin Case No. 107 of 1995 and he impugned order dated 15-9-2009 passed by the Joint District Judge 3rd Court Artha Rin Adalat Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2005 cannot be interfered by the revisional jurisdiction of this Court. 

 Accordingly, the Rules in Civil Revision Nos, 1919 of 2009 and 4232 of 2009 are discharged. The impugned judgment and order dated 23-4-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat Dhaka No.3 in Artha Rin Case No. 107 of 1995 and the judgment and order dated 19-5- 2009 passed by Ms Shahnaj Sultana, learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3 in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 2005 are here by affirmed.
